statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-41848 is a ReDoS in AntPathMatcher.doMatch when processing adversary-controlled path patterns with many trailing wildcards. Data Prepper 2.16.0 ships Spring Framework 5.3.39. The fix requires Spring 6.2.19 or 7.0.8, a major-version upgrade (javax to jakarta, Java 17 baseline) not yet adopted. The 5.3.x line is end-of-life and will not receive a backport. Monitoring for an adoptable fix or alternative mitigation.

CVE-2026-41848 is a ReDoS in AntPathMatcher.doMatch when processing adversary-controlled path patterns with many trailing wildcards. Data Prepper 2.16.0 ships Spring Framework 5.3.39. The fix requires Spring 6.2.19 or 7.0.8, a major-version upgrade (javax to jakarta, Java 17 baseline) not yet adopted. The 5.3.x line is end-of-life and will not receive a backport. Monitoring for an adoptable fix or alternative mitigation.

CVE-2024-38827 affects Spring Framework's authorization rules when using locale-dependent String.toLowerCase() and String.toUpperCase(). The fix requires Spring Framework 6.1.14, a major version jump from the current 5.3.39. Upgrading to Spring 6.x would require Java 17 baseline and significant API changes incompatible with Data Prepper's current architecture. The vulnerability requires an application to use Spring Security with locale-sensitive authorization rules. Data Prepper does not use Spring Security; authentication is handled via HTTP Basic in the management API configuration. Investigation ongoing for a backport or alternative mitigation.

CVE-2024-38827 is a Spring Security advisory (spring-security-core AuthorizationManager case-sensitivity). Data Prepper ships Spring Framework 5.3.39 but does not depend on Spring Security, so the vulnerable component is not present in the image.

CVE-2024-38827 is a Spring Security advisory (spring-security-core AuthorizationManager case-sensitivity). Data Prepper ships Spring Framework 5.3.39 but does not depend on Spring Security, so the vulnerable component is not present in the image.

Verified: the CVE affects Spring's @PreAuthorize / @PostAuthorize method-security path, which lives in spring-security-*.jar (not spring-core). Spring Security is not bundled in /usr/share/data-prepper/lib/ (no spring-security-*.jar present), and no data-prepper-*.jar references org/springframework/security/ or the AuthorizationManager / PreAuthorize / PostAuthorize types (verified by grepping every bundled data-prepper jar). The data-prepper management API uses HTTP Basic via authentication.http_basic in data-prepper-config.yaml, not Spring Security. The improper-authorization codepath cannot be reached because the AuthorizationManager flow is never wired in.
